clue.text: It can help us read awkward situation after strike

indicators.note: after says the awkward situation follows the word for strike in the answer

parts.note: to lam is to strike or thrash
a plight is a predicament

explanation.surface: Something helps us make sense of an awkward situation that followed a strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' here is to thrash, not a walkout; 'It can help us read' is a cryptic definition of a source of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Light from a lamp is what lets people see the page at night.

clue.text: Vital method of communicating most of story to Tom, say

parts.note: a story is a lie; most of it, losing the last letter, gives LI
a tom is a male cat, an example of a feline

explanation.surface: Telling most of a tale to a man called Tom is an essential way of keeping in touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom, say' is a definition by example: a tomcat is a feline.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope or connection on which survival depends, such as a diver's link to the surface.

clue.text: Put on the stand

explanation.surface: A witness is placed in the witness box.
explanation.definitionFit: To mount a show is to stage it; a mount is also the stand or backing an object is fixed to.

clue.text: Time trial organised? Exactly!

indicators.note: something organised has been put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cyclist asks whether the time trial was properly organised and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for letter by letter, meaning precisely word for word.

clue.text: For Scots around brae provide guide

indicators.note: around means the word for provide wraps about the hill

parts.note: gie is the Scots form of give, to provide
a brae is a Scottish hillside, so a hill

explanation.surface: Scottish walkers want someone to show them the way round a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For Scots' warns that the pieces are Scots words: GIE for give, and brae. A ghillie is a Highland hunting or fishing attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish attendant who leads sportsmen on fishing or stalking trips.

clue.text: Run up to a German and do a swap

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to dart is to run quickly
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: Dash up to a German man and exchange something with him.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade something in is to hand it over in part exchange for a replacement.

clue.text: Bring into play spades (king first) to make tricks

indicators.note: first says the king's letter goes at the front ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king
to bring something into play is to use it
S is the card abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A card player leads spades, with the king first, to win tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruses are deceptions or wiles, as tricks are.

clue.text: Female's left cold and stiff

indicators.note: left in the sense of having departed, so the female's letter goes

parts.note: frigid means very cold
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman went off, leaving the atmosphere chilly and stiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid means unbending or stiff.

clue.text: Quit, having lost blood — took off quickly

parts.note: scram is slang for clear off or quit
to bleed is to lose blood

explanation.surface: Someone who was wounded left and departed in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrambled can mean hurried off, especially of aircraft taking off at speed.

clue.text: In this way, raise level of spirits?

definitions.text: In this way, raise level of spirits?

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
to lace a drink is to add a spirit to it, raising its alcohol

explanation.surface: Someone suggests livening up a gloomy party by spiking the drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: comfort raises a person's spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfort in distress lifts a person's mood.

clue.text: Penalty in court for offence

explanation.surface: A judge hands down a punishment for a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a fault is a serve that is penalised; a fault is also a misdeed or offence.

clue.text: Maiden in part of summer briefly goes to river

parts.note: taken as written
August is part of summer, and AUG is its short form
the Ural is a river of Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A girl spends part of the summer by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' looks like a girl but is the adjective, as in a maiden speech or voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden voyage or speech is the first one, which is what an inaugural one is.

clue.text: It could provide a taller sideshoot

indicators.note: the letters of the answer could be rearranged to provide the following words, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A gardener hopes a side branch will grow taller.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a lateral is a shoot growing from the side of a stem.

clue.text: Half held in enclosure, confined to one area

indicators.note: held in means the word for half sits within the abbreviation

parts.note: ENC is the abbreviation for enclosure in letters
demi is a prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: Livestock are half kept in a pen, restricted to one patch.
explanation.definitionFit: Endemic describes a disease or species native to and restricted to a particular region.

clue.text: Ring may be risque

explanation.surface: Wearing a certain ring could be rather daring.
explanation.definitionFit: A finger ring sits close to the joint of the finger; the idiom also means bordering on indecent.

clue.text: Champion has a game point

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the gist is the main point of something

explanation.surface: A sporting winner owns a game point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' is not a winner here but one who champions a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: One who argues in defence of a cause or belief, as a champion does.

clue.text: Show approval of directors giving cover for house

parts.note: to clap is to applaud
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: Applauding the company's board for giving the firm protection.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlapping horizontal planks used as external siding on a building.

clue.text: Unusual type of service known by a marine

parts.note: under as in going under a name, being known by it
RM stands for Royal Marines

explanation.surface: An odd way of serving in tennis is identified by a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks military beside 'marine', but it is the serve in a ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: Serving with the hand below the shoulder is uncommon in serious tennis.

clue.text: Ordinary green and gold beds

parts.note: a village green is common land
or is the heraldic word for gold
flower beds make up a garden

explanation.surface: A garden scene of lawns, golden flowers and plant beds.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for plain, unremarkable and everyday.

clue.text: Method of feeding began so originally

indicators.note: read as in an original, inventive way, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A process of eating that started like this from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag of feed hung over a horse's head lets it eat.

clue.text: I arrive shattered in holiday destination

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into pieces, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A tourist turns up exhausted at their resort.
explanation.definitionFit: The French and Italian Mediterranean coast is a classic resort area.

clue.text: Support the Queen — it's only right

parts.note: a prop is a support
ER, for Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A loyal subject feels it fitting to back the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper means correct or fitting.

clue.text: Diamond ring maiden found in wild shrub

indicators.note: found in means the ring and maiden letters sit inside the rearranged plant
wild suggests disorder, so the letters of the plant are scrambled

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of O
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a lost diamond ring in an overgrown bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges SHRUB to RHBUS; O and M go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is the lozenge shape seen on playing cards as a diamond.

clue.text: The two year cover provided for farmworkers

parts.note: both means the two together

explanation.surface: A farm gives its labourers a two-year insurance policy.
explanation.walkthrough: A bothy is a basic hut, chiefly Scottish, used to house farm labourers.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple cottage or hut giving shelter to agricultural labourers.

clue.text: Tremble with struggle to restrain naughty child

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so the child sits inside the word for struggle

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle
a brat is a badly behaved child

explanation.surface: A parent shakes while trying to hold back an unruly youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: To vibrate is to shake or quiver.

clue.text: A Scandinavian keeled over in shock

indicators.note: keeled over means upended, so in this down clue the word is turned upside down

parts.note: a Lapp is a person from Lapland in northern Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A northern European collapses from fright.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to horrify or dismay.

clue.text: Fit enough to run

parts.note: run is read as a print run in a newspaper, not a race, so fit to go into print

explanation.surface: An athlete is just about well enough to race.
explanation.definitionFit: Decent enough to be published in a newspaper.

clue.text: Some unusual phantoms appear in the beginning

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Strange ghosts show up at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of the Greek alphabet stands for the start, as in alpha and omega.

clue.text: Irritable friend of Toad

explanation.surface: An amphibian has a grumpy companion.
explanation.walkthrough: Ratty is the Water Rat, Toad's friend in Kenneth Grahame's The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is slang for bad-tempered, and the name of the rat in the children's classic.

clue.text: Big noise's achievement in bridge world

parts.note: grand means large
a slam is a loud banging noise

explanation.surface: A loud bang marks a feat on the bridge circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning all thirteen tricks in bridge, and by extension winning all major titles in a sport.
